title: Rabbi Zemina
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman takes him to have been Rabbi Yonah’s colleague from [Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 3:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bikkurim.3.3.19), which describes both men: Rabbi Zemina was in Tyre, and they appointed him on condition that he return [to the Land of Israel]; Rabbi Yonah too was in Pitka and would not accept an appointment.

notes.text: In the Guggenheimer digital Jerusalem Talmud Bikkurim 3:3, appointment outside the Land is discussed on condition of returning. This supports return to the Land of Israel, rather than repayment. The inference that Zemina and Yonah were colleagues remains Hyman’s.
In the consulted Yerushalmi, Zemina’s appointment is conditional on his return. Hyman infers that he was Yonah’s colleague from the juxtaposition of the two accounts.

In [Bikkurim 3:3:19](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bikkurim.3.3.19), the rabbis of Caesarea permit appointment abroad on condition of return. Guggenheimer understands pitka in the next sentence as a list of candidates for appointment; Hyman’s wording is carried here as Pitka.
